topPRs.title: feat: re-add OPCM V800 templates with simplified super-permissioned args
topPRs.author: OptimismBot
topPRs.body:
> **Draft — do not merge until the V800 OPCM is deployed on-chain.**

Re-adds the `OPCMUpgradeV800` and `OPCMMigrateV800` templates, their integration tests, and example tasks that were removed in #1501, now carrying the simplified super-permissioned game arg layout from #1500.

Stacked on #1501 (base branch `centaur/remove-opcm-v800-templates`). GitHub will retarget this to `main` once #1501 merges.

## What changed vs the original V800 templates
`OPCMUpgradeV800` encodes `SUPER_PERMISSIONED_CANNON` (gt=5) game args as **proposer-only** (`abi.encode(a.proposer)`, 32 bytes) instead of the old `abi.encode(absolutePrestate, proposer, challenger)`, matching the simplified op-contracts V800 ABI. Test coverage in `SuperRootUpgrade.t.sol` is updated accordingly, and `test_upgrade_sepolia()` is dropped because the forked OPCM predates the new layout. This is the exact diff from #1500.

## Why draft
V800 is not yet deployed on-chain, so `template_regression_tests` cannot simulate `035-opcm-upgrade-v800` against a compatible OPCM — it reverts in `_build`. By removing the templates from `main` (#1501) and re-adding the new version here, we avoid carrying a backwards-compatibility shim for a not-yet-live OPCM. Once V800 is deployed: merge #1501, then mark this ready and merge.

Closes #1466 (once merged)

Prompted by: @mds1

topPRs.title: feat(template): add SetFeeVaultConfig for in-place fee-vault config updates
topPRs.author: donoso-eth
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds a reusable `SetFeeVaultConfig` template that updates the on-chain config
(recipient / withdrawalNetwork / minWithdrawalAmount) of one or more L2 fee-vault
predeploys **in place**, via the vaults' own owner-gated setters
(`setRecipient` / `setWithdrawalNetwork` / `setMinWithdrawalAmount`), sent as
`OptimismPortal2.depositTransaction` from the L1 ProxyAdminOwner. No proxy upgrade,
no re-initialize. Chain-specific values come from `config.toml`.

## Why

The existing fee-vault templates change the recipient by **upgrading the impl**
(`UpdateFeeVaultRecipient` installs a new immutable impl; `FeeVaultUpgradeTemplate`
migrates to the storage design via `initialize`). Once a chain's vaults are already on the
storage design (e.g. OP Sepolia / Ink Mainnet: L1FeeVault v1.6.1, OperatorFeeVault v1.1.1),
re-running `FeeVaultUpgradeTemplate` reverts (`InvalidInitialization`) and would downgrade
the impl. On those chains recipient/network/min are mutable storage with owner-gated
setters, so a plain setter call is the correct, minimal mechanism — which is what this
template provides.

### Files

- **`src/template/SetFeeVaultConfig.sol`** — `L2TaskBase` template; emits one portal
  deposit per *changed* field across the configured `vaultProxies`.
- **`test/tasks/example/sep/041-set-fee-vault-config/`** — example task (OP Sepolia:
  L1FeeVault + OperatorFeeVault → shared recipient, WithdrawalNetwork.L1).
- **`test/integration/SetFeeVaultConfigIntegration.t.sol`** — end-to-end test; forks
  L1 + OP Sepolia, replays the setter deposits, asserts the vault config changed. Reuses
  `IntegrationBase`.

### Validation

- **Capability/version gate** — rejects vaults below the min version that exposes the
  setters (Sequencer/Base/L1 ≥ 1.6.0, Operator ≥ 1.1.1); old immutable vaults must use
  `FeeVaultUpgradeTemplate` first.
- **Required `l2RpcUrls` preflight** — asserts `L2 ProxyAdmin.owner() == aliased root`,
  enforces the version gate, and **dry-runs the setters** as the aliased owner so an L2
  revert surfaces at setup instead of silently on relay.
- **Per-field skip-unchanged** — only fields that differ from live state produce a deposit;
  at least one must change (else the framework reverts "No actions found").
- **`_validate`** — asserts action count + every action targets the OptimismPortal, value 0.
- Non-zero recipient, `network <= 1`, and known-vault checks.

## Test plan

- [x] `forge test --match-test test_setFeeVaultConfig_integration -vvv` — 1/1 passed (4/4 deposits succeed; recipient/network/min verified on the OP Sepolia fork)
- [x] `just simulate` on `sep/041` — `SETFEEVAULTCONFIG: VALIDATED PORTAL DEPOSIT ACTIONS`
- [x] `forge build --deny-warnings` — clean
- [x] `forge fmt --check` — clean
- [x] `./src/script/check-struct-order.sh` — clean

## Self-review (template-review checklist)

Ran the internal template-review checklist; **0 blocking findings**. Minor items resolved:
inline interfaces (`IOptimismPortal2`/`IProxyAdminView`/`IVersioned`), `vm.label`s, corrected
NatSpec (the "No actions found" behavior + skip-unchanged sign-time semantics), removed an
unused import, `Supports:` line added. `_taskStorageWrites = ["OptimismPortalProxy"]`
cross-checked against the sim state diff.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Escalation:** this is a **new template type** and performs a **cross-layer** operation
> (L1→L2 portal deposits driving L2 setter calls) — flagged for **Security-team review** per
> the template-review checklist.

## Notes

- Additive: does not modify `UpdateFeeVaultRecipient` or `FeeVaultUpgradeTemplate`.
- No `Regression.t.sol` entry: per-field skip-unchanged reads live L2 state, so a
  hardcoded-calldata regression test would be non-deterministic. The `sep/041` example is
  covered by CI's `simulate-all-templates`, and the integration test covers the end-to-end
  L2 effect — matching the sibling `UpdateFeeVaultRecipient`, which likewise has no
  regression test.

topPRs.title: Allow new Safe owners to presign follow-up tasks
topPRs.author: mds1
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds an explicit `SKIP_SIGNER_OWNER_CHECK=true|1` override to the shared `TaskManager` signing preflight. This lets a new Safe owner presign a follow-up task before the earlier owner-addition task executes; the owner check remains enabled by default.

The bypass still rejects a zero signer or codeless target and calls `getOwners()` to validate the Safe interface. It skips only owner membership and prints a warning with the signer and Safe addresses. A recursive policy test rejects `SKIP_SIGNER_OWNER_CHECK` in every tracked task `.env`, so the exception stays command-scoped.

## Why

Sequential owner rotations intentionally require a newly added owner to sign a later task. For example, `056-fus-rotation-1` adds an owner that must sign `057-fus-rotation-2`, but the existing preflight reads current onchain ownership and blocks that signature until `056` executes.

## Validation

- `mise exec -- forge fmt --check`
- `mise exec -- forge test --match-contract TaskManagerUnitTest --match-test 'test(RequireSignerOnSafe|TaskEnvFiles_DoNotContainSkipSignerOwnerCheck)' -vv` (`2/2` pass)
- `FOUNDRY_PROFILE=ci mise exec -- forge build`
- `git diff origin/main...HEAD --check`
- Independent spec/quality, security/operations, test, and whole-branch reviews completed with no open findings

## Additional context

The override skips only the current-owner preflight. Simulation, transaction construction, hash validation, hardware-wallet signing, and execution-time signature validation are unchanged.

topPRs.title: fix: preserve Safe owners in simulation overrides
topPRs.author: mds1
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Preserve the Safe's real owner links when adding the synthetic simulation owner. The override now appends that owner and increments `ownerCount` instead of replacing the real owner list, which fixes Tenderly simulations that rotate the first owner.

This only changes simulation authentication state. The simulated list has one extra owner, but remains internally consistent; task calldata, Safe transaction hashes, signatures, and onchain state are unchanged. Tasks that depend on the exact owner count or enumerate owners still require a different simulation strategy.

## Validation

- `forge test --match-contract StateOverrideManagerUnitTest --match-test test_getStateOverrides_appendsSimulationOwnerWithoutReplacingOwnerList -vv`

topPRs.title: docs: mark eth tasks 056-059 as EXECUTED
topPRs.author: OptimismBot
topPRs.body:
## What

Marks four executed OP Mainnet governance tasks as `EXECUTED` in their task READMEs, linking each to its on-chain execution transaction. Docs-only change (no Solidity/config/validation edits).

The signer rotations on the Foundation Upgrade Safe (056, 057) and Foundation Operations Safe (058, 059) were executed on mainnet.

| Task | Tx |
|------|----|
| `eth/056-fus-rotation-1` | [`0xbb0cece7…`](https://etherscan.io/tx/0xbb0cece7d5f45ce07894be038b83af893b894a3337a5dda22b79b46097c4ce96) |
| `eth/057-fus-rotation-2` | [`0x087cbb21…`](https://etherscan.io/tx/0x087cbb21ebc9739c7afed878236a9cba9b1e129adc6a976fefe5571b88452ce8) |
| `eth/058-fos-rotation-1` | [`0xd3a6afee…`](https://etherscan.io/tx/0xd3a6afeef57d1e1b7fde86a4b0dd5de6fb6747cec75d6d9edecf54e7eacb19ea) |
| `eth/059-fos-rotation-2` | [`0x86366bc8…`](https://etherscan.io/tx/0x86366bc8466b0b45ece66d277ec47f988cfad38a3147c6d71b623e104d9d2ab5) |

Each README's status line changes from `Status: [READY TO SIGN]()` to `Status: [EXECUTED](<tx-url>)`, following the same convention as #1494 and #1457.

## Agent skill

Also adds `.claude/skills/mark-task-executed/SKILL.md` so agents can perform this status-update-and-PR flow quickly and cheaply going forward, documenting the status-line convention, the network→explorer mapping, and the verification/PR steps.

## Review notes

Reviewers should confirm each tx hash on Etherscan corresponds to the intended task execution (correct Safe, correct calldata).
